title: Zakariyya's silence
hook: his sign is three days without speaking except by gesture, and remembering Allah (3:41)
tomorrow: Maryam above the women of the worlds

segments.voice: Yesterday, istafa, the chosen family: Adam, Nuh, the family of Ibrahim and the family of Imran. Your line was a chosen line. Did you pass something on to someone younger? Day three hundred sixty-six.

An old man walks into a small prayer room to check on the girl he's raising. She's Maryam, and he's her guardian, Zakariyya. He finds food beside her, and it's food he didn't bring. Where did this come from, he asks. From God, she says; God provides for whom He wills, beyond counting. And the old man, who has no children and a wife who never could, stands right there and starts to pray for a child of his own.
screen: `A SMALL PRAYER ROOM.` → `FOOD HE DIDN'T BRING.` → `AN OLD MAN STARTS TO PRAY.`

segments.voice: That's 3:37 and 38. The prayer room is called the mihrab, the same word used today for the niche in a mosque's wall that shows the direction of prayer. What Zakariyya saw in Maryam's room made him brave enough to ask. Then, 3:39: while he's still standing in prayer, the angels call to him with good news of a son, Yahya, who will confirm a word from God, and be noble, chaste, and a prophet. And Zakariyya, who has just asked for exactly this, asks how. I'm old. My wife is barren. The answer, in Pickthall's words: "So (it will be). Allah doeth what He will." So he asks for a sign. And the sign is strange. In 3:41 he's told he won't speak to people for three days, except by ramz, by gesture. And then: remember your Lord much, and glorify Him in the evening and the morning. In Surah Maryam, chapter nineteen, the same sign is given as three nights, and there he comes out and signals to his people to glorify God morning and evening. Commentators differ on why it came this way. Some read the silence as a mercy, a sign he could feel in his own body. Others note that his tongue was stopped from talk with people, but never from remembering God. Christians tell a story of the same man, Zechariah, in the Gospel of Luke. Here, in the Qur'an's telling, the point lands on what filled the silence. Three days with no small talk, no explaining, no complaining. Only gestures, and dhikr, remembrance, morning and evening.
screen: `THE MIHRAB: FOOD HE DIDN'T BRING` · `GOOD NEWS OF YAHYA` · `RAMZ: THREE DAYS OF GESTURE` · `A SILENCE FULL OF REMEMBRANCE` · then, large: `ALLAH DOETH WHAT HE WILL.`

segments.voice: Try a short version of Zakariyya's sign. Later today, if you can, take a quiet hour: no talking, no messages, gestures only if someone needs you. For now, when the bell starts, close your mouth gently and let the silence settle. Notice how much talk runs inside you even when you aren't speaking. Each time a sentence starts to form, let it go, and come back to one simple remembrance. If you pray, that can be subhanallah, glory be to God. If you don't, simply the breath. The bell holds the time.
Zakariyya's silence. Three days without speech, only gesture, filled with remembrance, morning and evening. Today's word.
Your line: silent and remembering. Today, when you'd normally fill a pause with talk, leave it empty for a moment, and let one quiet remembrance take its place. Day three hundred sixty-six.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Zakariyya and Yahya as prophets; his story (3:37–41 and Surah Maryam) is often recited by those hoping for a child, and his sign of silence filled with remembrance is a model for quiet dhikr in the morning and evening.

fork.setup: you're Zakariyya. the angels have just told you you'll have a son, though you're old. you ask for a sign. what is it?
options: you won't speak to people for three days, except by gesture.

fork.reveal: three days of silence, speaking only by gesture, and remembering God much, evening and morning (3:41).

original.note: Arabic: by gesture, by sign (3:41); the only way Zakariyya spoke to people for three days.

trapdoor: what you thought: he lost his voice as a punishment.
what it means: in the Qur'an's telling, the silence is the sign he asked for, filled with remembrance of God.
what a scholar hears: ramz, gesture; three days in 3:41 and three nights in 19:10, read together by commentators as one sign of full days and nights.
